title: Hypersonic missile startup Castelion raises $1 billion
summary: Hypersonic missile startup Castelion, founded by former SpaceX executives, raised $1 billion to develop low-cost hypersonic weapons and a broader portfolio of strike and missile defense systems.

title: Eartheye Space forges strategic partnership with IN2
summary: Eartheye Space has formed a strategic partnership with risk-management firm IN2, granting IN2 access to Eartheye's multi-sensor satellite data and analytics through a memorandum of understanding signed on August 19.

title: Katalyst Space and NASA abandon plans for Swift reboost
summary: Katalyst Space and NASA have canceled plans to use Katalyst's Link spacecraft to boost the orbit of NASA's Swift gamma-ray observatory due to attitude-control issues with the spacecraft.

title: Moog Inc. Expands METEORITE Satellite Bus Capacity for High-Maneuverability Missions
summary: Moog Inc. has expanded the capacity of its METEORITE satellite bus to support high-maneuverability missions. The announcement highlights the company's advancements in satellite technology.

title: The space industry’s next challenge: supply chain resilience
summary: The space industry is facing supply chain resilience challenges as its economy scales faster than its industrial base can support. Commercial constellations, national security architectures, and civil missions are all contributing to increased demand.

title: Vantor names new head of U.S. government business
summary: Vantor has appointed Will Cocos as the new executive vice president and general manager of its U.S. government business, succeeding Susanne Hake. The company is part of the Earth intelligence sector.

title: Firefly Aerospace to fly Zeno Power radioisotope heating unit on lunar lander mission
summary: Firefly Aerospace will carry a Zeno Power radioisotope heating unit on a lunar lander mission to test a heat source for surviving the lunar night. This collaboration aims to enable future lunar missions to endure extreme cold conditions.

title: Space nuclear programs face near- and long-term challenges
summary: Space nuclear programs are currently gaining attention but face both immediate and long-term challenges. Industry officials highlight these hurdles despite the growing interest.

title: China’s Landspace recovers booster with second  orbital launch of Zhuque-3 rocket
summary: Landspace successfully recovered the first stage of its Zhuque-3 rocket after its second orbital launch from the Gobi Desert. This marks a significant milestone in China's reusable rocket development.

title: Rocket Lab to test Space Force data network connection in orbit in 2027
summary: Rocket Lab will test a connection to the U.S. Space Force's data network in orbit in 2027 using a Photon spacecraft. The test aims to assess interoperability with SpaceX's Space Data Network infrastructure.

title: Scientists just found the fastest known star in the Milky Way. It zooms around our black hole at 15,500 miles per second
summary: Scientists discovered the fastest known star in the Milky Way, traveling at 15,500 miles per second around the supermassive black hole Sagittarius A*. The star orbits the black hole at the galaxy's center.

title: Private mission to save NASA's Swift space telescope fails
summary: A private spacecraft mission aimed at extending the orbit of NASA's Swift space telescope has failed, leading to its expected reentry and crash later this year.

title: Scientists create 'laundry gun' for astronauts to clean their clothes by shooting out plasma
summary: Scientists have developed a pen-sized 'laundry gun' that uses plasma to sterilize astronauts' clothes in space. This innovation aims to address the challenge of laundry in microgravity environments.

title: 'The Mandalorian and Grogu' finally blasts onto Disney+ next month
summary: The Mandalorian and Grogu spinoff will launch on Disney+ next month, potentially reviving the underwhelming series. The streaming debut may determine the future of the franchise.

title: Dark matter could magnify the jets of a ravenously feeding supermassive black hole
summary: A jet from a distant supermassive black hole-powered blazar is being gravitationally lensed by an unseen clump of dark matter, potentially revealing the source of cosmic 'ghost' particles.

title: A SpaceX rocket slammed into the moon this month — and a NASA spacecraft has spotted its lunar grave (photos)
summary: A SpaceX rocket stage crashed into the moon in March 2022, creating a 60-foot-wide crater. NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter later identified the impact site in images.

title: Mysterious Russian 'space activity' causes US Air Force flight to Antarctica to turn around: report
summary: A U.S. Air Force flight to Antarctica was forced to turn around due to a possible space debris hazard caused by mysterious Russian 'space activity' over the South Pacific on Aug. 18.

title: Perseverance rover watches alien solar eclipse on Mars | Space photo of the day for Aug. 19, 2026
summary: NASA's Perseverance rover captured a stunning image of a solar eclipse on Mars. The event showcased Phobos, one of Mars' moons, passing in front of the Sun.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 19, 1997: 1st Filipino satellite launches into orbit
summary: On Aug. 19, 1997, the Philippines launched its first satellite into orbit. This marked a significant milestone for the country's space program.

title: NASA TechLeap Prize: Orbital Clarity Challenge
summary: NASA's TechLeap Prize introduces the Orbital Clarity Challenge to address space weather impacts on Earth's atmosphere. The challenge is a collaboration between NASA's Heliophysics Division, Flight Opportunities program, and Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation.

title: NASA Updates Next Steps for Commercial Swift Boost Mission
summary: NASA and Katalyst Space have postponed the LINK spacecraft's planned satellite boost mission due to an ongoing attitude control issue. However, LINK will still attempt rendezvous and proximity operations with NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory.

title: Human-Related Microbes May Survive Moon’s South Pole, NASA Finds
summary: NASA research suggests that microbes from Earth could survive in shaded areas of the Moon's South Pole, raising concerns about potential contamination during human exploration. The findings, published in Science Advances, underscore the need for better understanding of microbial persistence in lunar environments.

title: Ancient Milky Way Merger
summary: A study using NASA's Hubble Space Telescope revealed evidence of a dwarf galaxy, LKH, merging with the young Milky Way around 12 billion years ago. The findings, published in Nature Astronomy, provide insights into the ancient history of our galaxy.

title: NASA Establishes State Hubs to Grow Technical Aerospace Workforce
summary: NASA has allocated $10.5 million to seven institutions to enhance state-based pathways for students entering technical aerospace careers. The initiative aims to strengthen the skilled workforce in the aerospace industry.

title: Behind the Lens: Meet NASA Johnson’s Photographers
summary: NASA Johnson Space Center photographers document key moments in human spaceflight, preserving history and showcasing the teams behind missions. Their work highlights astronaut training, engineering tests, and mission control operations.

title: APOD: 2026 August 19 – The Case of the Mysterious Maybe Meteor
summary: APOD (Astronomy Picture of the Day) features a daily image or photograph of the universe with an explanation by an astronomer. The featured content for August 19, 2026, is titled 'The Case of the Mysterious Maybe Meteor'.

title: NASA’s LRO Images Falcon 9 Crater on Moon, Learns New Details
summary: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) captured images of a new crater on the Moon formed by a SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage impact on Aug. 5, following its January 2025 launch of the Firefly Blue Ghost 1 mission.

title: NASA Student Aviation Challenge Focuses on Nation’s Infrastructure
summary: NASA's Gateways to Blue Skies competition challenges college teams to design aircraft for inspecting infrastructure like bridges and tunnels by 2035. The goal is to enhance safety, reliability, and cost-efficiency in national infrastructure.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine assembly for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch around 2026. This positions Stoke Space as a competitor in the fully reusable launch vehicle market alongside SpaceX's Starship.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, successfully completed its second flight and achieved the first-stage landing. This milestone marks a significant advancement for the company in reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location near Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 lunar mission following a recent launch failure of the Chang Zheng 7A rocket. The mission is part of a series of launches alongside SpaceX's Starlink deployments.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also progressing on its Eclipse program. The company is promoting its upcoming Alpha rocket block amid ongoing development efforts.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual launch pad operations at Cape Canaveral while restoring its primary pad at LC-36A. The company has shared details about its operational expansion plans.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. These moves expand the company's global presence and launch capabilities.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site celebrated its 50th launch milestone while also experiencing a failure. The site launched AI satellites and is preparing for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is progressing with the assembly of multiple Starship vehicles for future missions. The development aligns with SpaceX's long-term goals for Starship production and deployment.

title: Launch Preview: Chinese failure opens busy international launch salvo
summary: A Chinese launch failure on Aug. 10 preceded a busy week of international launches across three countries. The incident highlighted the challenges in spaceflight amid a high-frequency launch schedule.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates its 50th anniversary by releasing a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over the past five decades. The publication underscores the agency's milestones and contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise formation-flying capabilities.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona, which is otherwise difficult to study due to the rarity and brevity of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, a deep space asteroid mission. This offers a unique opportunity to test software in deep space millions of kilometers away.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESA's ESTEC technical centre in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's disk, simulating an eclipse. The mission involves two satellites playing a 'hide and seek' game to achieve this.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: White House Publishes S&T Strategy for National Security
summary: The White House released its National Security Science & Technology Strategy through the Office of Science and Technology Policy. This strategy aims to guide national security efforts in science and technology.
company: Office of Science and Technology Policy

title: Zeno Power Books its First Nuclear Mission to the Moon
summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial payload agreement with Firefly Aerospace to send a radioisotope heating unit to the Moon by 2028. The mission, part of Firefly's CS-8 CLPS mission, aims to demonstrate Zeno's technology for lunar applications.

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The U.S. Space Force's FY27 budget request has been announced, reaching a record $71.3 billion. This budget highlights significant investments in defense space capabilities.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace has enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered capabilities to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in managing satellite operations more effectively.

title: HEO Taps Planet Labs to Expand its NEI Network
summary: HEO has partnered with Planet Labs to expand its NEI network to over 50 in-space sensors, enabling more frequent and high-resolution imaging of objects in orbit from multiple angles.

title: DIU, SDA Select Winners for Deorbit-as-a-Service Designs
summary: The Space Development Agency (SDA) and Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) selected three companies to design scalable satellite capabilities for rendezvous, capture, and deorbit services. This initiative aims to address space debris mitigation through a 'Deorbit-as-a-Service' approach.
company: Space Development Agency (SDA) and Defense Innovation Unit (DIU)

title: SEOPS Doubles Down on Waymaker Dedicated Rideshare Program
summary: SEOPS is expanding its Waymaker dedicated rideshare program as SpaceX's Transporter program ends, aiming to provide cost-effective rides to orbit for space startups.

title: The New Middle Ground in Spacecraft Development
summary: The commercial space industry is shifting towards customers building their own spacecraft hardware for full mission ownership. This trend represents a new middle ground in spacecraft development beyond affordability and accessibility.

title: Exclusive: Reflect Orbital Responds to its Critics
summary: Reflect Orbital faces criticism over its sunlight-reflecting satellites, with the space community divided on the idea. The company has responded to these concerns.

title: NASA Opens Call on Moon Base Health Research
summary: NASA's Human Research Program is soliciting research proposals to address health challenges for long-term stays at a Moon Base. The initiative aims to gather critical data for future lunar missions.

title: TGS Taps Speedcast for All-LEO Solution
summary: Speedcast has secured a connectivity deal with TGS, a global provider of data and intelligence, to implement an all-LEO solution across its fleet. This marks another win for Speedcast in the energy industry.

title: Will Cocos to Lead Vantor’s US Government Business
summary: Vantor has appointed Will Cocos as executive vice president and general manager to lead its U.S. government business, focusing on defense, intelligence, and civil sectors.

title: Katalyst Link Mission is Unable to Rescue NASA Swift Observatory
summary: The Katalyst Link mission, a space servicing mission launched to rescue NASA's Swift Observatory, has been confirmed unable to complete the rescue by NASA and Katalyst. The mission aimed to extend the lifespan of the Swift Observatory but failed in its objective.

title: Kratos Reports Growing Tri-Band Antenna Demand and Debuts New Model
summary: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions has secured multi-million-dollar orders for GAIA antenna systems from international customers. The company also debuted a new model to meet growing tri-band antenna demand.

title: The Rogue Element: How Transnational Cartels Could Establish an Asymmetric Lunar Presence
summary: The Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies warns the U.S. Space Force about potential 'in-person' lunar conflict with China, highlighting concerns over transnational cartels establishing an asymmetric lunar presence.

title: Delta Incident Puts Aviation Cybersecurity into Sharp Focus
summary: A recent incident involving Delta Airlines has highlighted the critical importance of cybersecurity in aviation in-flight connectivity (IFC) systems. The event underscores ongoing concerns in the satellite industry about securing passenger and operational communications.

title: Viasat Taps Rocket Lab to Build Small GEO for PTS-G Program
summary: Viasat has selected Rocket Lab to construct a small Geostationary Orbit (GEO) satellite for its Protected Tactical Satcom-Global (PTS-G) program. The spacecraft will be based on Rocket Lab's platform.

title: Vietnam’s VinSpace Plans to Launch Tech Demonstration on 2027 SpaceX Rideshare Mission
summary: VinSpace, a subsidiary of Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup, has signed a launch contract with SpaceX to send tech demonstration satellites on a 2027 Transporter rideshare mission. This marks a significant step for Vietnam's emerging space sector.

title: Aerospace Report Examines Defense and Space Growth in FY ‘27 Budget Request
summary: A new report from The Aerospace Corporation analyzes the White House's FY 2027 budget request, highlighting that over 75% of the increase is allocated to defense and space sectors.

title: L3Harris Appoints Sam Mehta as New CEO After Kubasik Forced Out Due to Conduct
summary: L3Harris Technologies appointed Sam Mehta as its new president and CEO, replacing Chris Kubasik who was forced out due to conduct issues. The leadership change was effective immediately.
